label: copy-phase input of digit 0
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, when the input token (the model own fed-back output) is the digit 0. It covers essentially all activation mass (dev recall 1.00, mass recall 1.00), with only 3 tiny misses on other tokens. It never fires in the original or delimiter phases, including when 0 appears among the original tokens, and never on any other token. About 24% of copy-phase 0 inputs stay inactive, and no simple variable explains which ones. The rate is lower at recall_idx 1 (0 fed back right after <DEL>, 1.5%) than at recall_idx >= 3 (about 2.8%). The rate is also higher when the sequence has more digits or starts with 0. The largest activations occur when 0 is fed back early in the copy (recall_idx 1-3) of long sequences, e.g. l d 0 0 v v d v <DEL> l d [0].

issues: The core predicate holds. On test it misses 0 activations, and on dev it misses 3 of 69,139 active steps. The feature never fires outside the copy phase. Mass recall is 1.00 and correlation is 0.74. The label 'copy-phase input of digit 0' does not overclaim.

The claim that firing is 'more common in sequences with more digits' is reversed once you look only at copy-phase 0 inputs, which is the population the predicate covers. Precision is 0.79 when n_digits==1, 0.73 when n_digits>=2 and 0.69 when n_digits>=3. The profile's rising rate only reflects that sequences with more digits contain more 0 inputs.

The claim that firing is 'more common in sequences that start with 0' is also reversed on the same population. Precision is 0.51 when first_tok==0 and 0.82 when first_tok!=0. A sequence that starts with 0 feeds the 0 back at recall_idx 1, which is the weak position. The explanation does say these numbers come from the all-steps profile, but it still states the wrong direction for both claims.

The recall_idx 1 claim checks out. Precision is 0.46 at recall_idx 1 and 0.82 at recall_idx >= 2. Short sequences behave the same way: precision is 0.48 when L <= 4. There is also a pattern the explanation does not mention: a 0 fed back on the last step (to_go == 0) fires with precision 0.84.

The false positives in the misses output (dev and test) look scattered across letters, positions and lengths, apart from the recall_idx 1 / short-L dip. For example, step 5 of '0 s e q <DEL> 0 s e' is inactive. The roughly 22% of copy-phase 0 inputs that never fire remain unexplained, but no single token, position, length or history pattern accounts for them.

One refinement gives a small gain: dropping the cases where L <= 4 and recall_idx == 1. Dev F1 rises from 0.862 to 0.871 and test F1 from 0.863 to 0.872, with recall staying at 0.99. The baseline predicate is therefore close to the best simple one.
